questions.q: A force $\overset{→}{F} = ( 40\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} ) N$ acts on a body of mass $5$ kg. If the body starts from rest, its position vector $\overset{→}{r}$ at time $t = 10s$& will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{d\overset{→}{v}}{dt} = \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{F}m = ( 8\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} ) ms^{- 2}$

$\dfrac{d\overset{→}{r}}{dt} = \overset{→}{v} = ( 8t\overset{^}{i} + 2t\overset{^}{j} ) ms^{- 1}$

$\overset{→}{r} = ( \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} ) \dfrac{t2}{2}m$

At~$t = 10sec$

$\overset{→}{r} = [ ( 8\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} ) 50 ] m$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r} = ( 400\overset{^}{i} + 100\overset{^}{j} ) m$

questions.q: A body of weight $200 \mathrm{~N}$ is suspended from a tree branch through a chain of mass $10 \mathrm{~kg}$. The branch pulls the chain by a force equal to (if $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Chain block system is in equilibrium so $\mathrm{T}=200+100=300 \mathrm{~N} \text {. }$

questions.q: A mass $m$ is attached to two springs as shown in figure. The spring constants of two springs are ${K}_{1}$~and ${K}_{2} .$~For the frictionless surface, the time period of oscillation of mass $m$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the given combination, if the block is displaced towards right, elongation in one spring will be equal to the compression in other and the direction of force due to both spring will be the same and restoring in nature. Hence, both& springs are effectively in parallel combination.

Therefore,

$⇒ {K}_{eff} = {K}_{1} + {K}_{2}$~and

$⇒ T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{Keff}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}}}$

questions.q: A block of mass $2$ kg moving on a horizontal surface with speed of $4\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ enters a rough surface ranging from $x = 0 . 5m$ to $x = 1 . 5m$. The retarding force in this range of rough surface is related to distance by $F = - kx$ where $k = 12Nm^{- 1}$. The speed of the block as it just crosses the rough surface will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the block& $a = \dfrac{f}{m} = - \dfrac{12x}{2} = - 6x$~(Here the block is retarding)

Now, using,~$a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$
$⇒ vdv = adx$
On integrating, we get

~${∫}_{4}^{v}v d v = - 6{∫}_{0 . 5}^{1 . 5}x d x$

$⇒ \dfrac{v^{2} - {4}^{2}}{2} = - 6 \left(\dfrac{ \left($1 . 5\right)2 - \left(0 . 5\right)2}{2}\right)

$⇒ v^{2} = 16 - 12 ⇒ v = 2ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: The normal reaction $N$~for a vehicle of $800$ kg mass, negotiating a turn on a $30 °$ banked road at maximum possible speed without skidding is ____~$\times {10}^{3}kgms^{- 2}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At ${v}_\max, f$ will be limiting in nature.

$∴$ Balancing force in vertical direction, $Ncos30 ° - mg - \muNcos60 ° = 0$
$⇒ N\left[cos30 ° - \mucos60 °\right] = mg$
$∴ N = \dfrac{800 \times 10}{( 0 . 87 - 0 . 1 )} \approx 10 . 2 \times {10}^{3}kgms^{- 2}$
Hence, option~$1 .$

questions.q:
A block of mass $5$ kg is (i) pushed in case \left(A\right)$ and (ii) pulled in case \left(B\right),$ by a force $F = 20N,$ making an angle of ${30}^{o}$ with the horizontal, as shown in the figures. The coefficient of friction between the block and floor is $\mu = 0.2 .$ The difference between the accelerations of the block, in case \left(B\right)$ and case \left(A\right)$ will be:
\left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For Block A:

$N = mg + Fsin ⁡ 30 °$
$= 5 \times 10 + 20 \times \dfrac{1}{2}$
$= 60N$
${f}_{r} = \left(0.2\right)\left(60\right) = 12N$
$Fcos ⁡ 30 ° – {f}_{r} = ma$
$20\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}- 12 = 5 \times a$
$⇒ {a}_{A} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3} - 12}{5}$ ……(i)
For Block B:

$Fsin ⁡ 30 ° + N = mg$
$N = 5 \times 10 – 20 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)
$= 40N$
${f}_{r} = 0.2 $\times$40 = 8N$
$Fcos30 ° – {f}_{r} = ma$
$20\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) -$8 = 5 $\times$a$
$⇒ {a}_{B} = $\dfrac{10\sqrt{3} - 8}{5}
${a}_{B} - {a}_{A} = $\dfrac{4}{5} =$0.8m / s^{2}$

questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg is suspended with the help of two strings making angles as shown in figure. Magnitude of tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$, respectively, are (in N) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1=\mathrm{mg} \cos 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \\ & \mathrm{T}_2=\mathrm{mg} \sin 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is fixed to one end of a light spring having force constant $k$ and unstretched length $l .$ The other end is fixed. The system is given an angular speed $\omega$ about the fixed end of the spring such that it rotates in a circle in gravity free space. Then the stretch in the spring is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, the spring force will give the necessary centripetal force for rotation.

So,&

$m{ω}^{2}\left(l + x\right) = kx$
\left(\dfrac{l}{x} + 1\right) = \dfrac{k}{m{ω}^{2}}$

~Thus, the stretch in the spring
$x = \dfrac{lm{ω}^{2}}{k - m{ω}^{2}}$

$

questions.q:
A system of two blocks of masses $m = 2kg$ and $M = 8kg$ is placed on a smooth table as shown in figure. The coefficient of static friction between two blocks is $0 . 5$. The maximum horizontal force $F$ that can be applied to the block of mass $M$ so that the blocks move together will be~ \left(g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Maximum acceleration of the upper block will be,

${a}_\max = \mug = 0 . 5 \times 9 . 8 = 4 . 9ms^{- 2}$

Therefore, maximum force that can be applied on the lower block is,

${F}_\max = \left(2 + 8\right) \times 4 . 9 = 49N$

questions.q: A train is moving with a speed of $12ms^{- 1}$ on rails which are $1 . 5m$ apart. To negotiate a curve radius $400m$, the height by which the outer rail should be raised with respect to the inner rail is (Given, $g =10ms^{- 2}$):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the train, moving along the curved rails, it can be written, with reference to the figure below, that

$tan\theta = \dfrac{v2}{Rg} . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, from the above figure, it follows that

$tan\theta = $\dfrac{h}{1 . 5} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

\dfrac{h}{1 . 5} = \dfrac{v2}{Rg}$⇒ h = 1 . 5 \times $\dfrac{v^{2}}{Rg} =$1 . 5 \times $\dfrac{\left(12ms^{- 1}\right)2}{400m \times 10ms^{- 2}} =$0 . 054m = 5 . 4cm$

$

questions.q: A car is moving with a constant speed of $20ms^{- 1}$ in a circular horizontal track of radius $40m$. A bob is suspended from the roof of the car by a massless string. The angle made by the string with the vertical will be : (Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f ( x ) = e^{x}sinx$

We know that the slope of tangent is given by~\left\{\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f^{'}\left(x\right)\right\}$.

Now,

$f^{'} ( x ) = Z = e^{x}sinx + e^{x}cosx$

$Z = e^{x} \left(sinx + cosx\right)$

\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$e^{x} \left(sinx + cosx\right) + e^{x} \left(cosx - sinx\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$2e^{x}cosx$

For maxima,~\dfrac{dZ}{dx} =$0$

$⇒ 2e^{x}cosx = 0$

$⇒ e^{x}cosx = 0$

$∵ e^{x} \ne 0, x \in R$~

$∴ cosx = 0 ⇒ x = $\dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$; \left\{∵ x \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]\right\}$

Now,~

$⇒ $\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}} =$2e^{x}cosx - 2e^{x}sinx$

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ \text{ and } \text{ and } \text{ and } $= 2e^{x} \left($cosx - sinx\right)$

\left$\${\$left(\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}}\right)$x = $\dfrac{π}{2}\right$\} = $-2e\dfrac{π}{2}< 0 \to \text{MAXIMA}$

And,~\left\{\left(\dfrac{d^{2}Z}{dx^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right\} = 2e\dfrac{3\pi}{2} > 0 \to \text{MINIMA}$

Hence,~$Z = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \left(\text{slope of tangent}\right)~is maximum when~$x = \dfrac{π}{2}.$

questions.q: A block kept on a rough inclined plane, as shown in the figure, remains at rest upto a maximum force $2N$ down the inclined plane. The maximum external force up the inclined plane that does not move the block is $10N .$ The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is: [Take $g = 10m / s^{2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$2 + mgsin ⁡ \theta = \mumgcos ⁡ \theta$

$mgsin ⁡ \theta - \mumgcos ⁡ \theta = 2 . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$
$mgsin ⁡ \theta + \mumgcos⁡ \theta =10 . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

equation (1) devided by (2)

$\dfrac{mg\left(sin ⁡ \theta - \mucos ⁡ \theta\right)}{mg\left(sin ⁡ \theta + \mucos ⁡ \theta\right)} = \dfrac{- 2}{10} = \dfrac{- 1}{5}$

\left(1 - \$mu\sqrt{3}\right)$5 = - \left(1 + \mu\sqrt{3}\right)$

$6 = 4\sqrt{3}\mu$

$\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

questions.q: A coin placed on a rotating table just slips when it is placed at a distance of $1$ cm from the centre. If the angular velocity of the table is halved, it will just slip when placed at a distance of _____ from the centre:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The coin will slip when&

$\mumg = m{ω}^{2}r$

$⇒ \mug = {ω}^{2} \times 1cm . . . ( i )$

Now,~$\omega ' = \dfrac{ω}{2}$

$\mug = \left(\dfrac{ω}{2}\right)2R . . . ( ii )$

Hence we can write from (i) and (ii)

${ω}^{2} \times 1cm = \dfrac{\omega2}{4}R ⇒ R = 4cm$

questions.q: An object with mass 500 g moves along x -axis with speed $v=4 \sqrt{x} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The force acting on the object is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & F=M \times a \\ & v=4 \sqrt{x} \\ & v^2=16 x \\ & 2 v \frac{d v}{d x}=16 \\ & \frac{v d v}{d x}=\frac{16}{2}=8 \\ & F=0.5 \times 8=4 N\end{aligned}$

questions.q: One end of a massless spring of spring constant $k$~and natural length ${l}_{0}$ is fixed while the other end is connected to a small object of mass $m$ lying on a frictionless table. The spring remains horizontal on the table. If the object is made to rotate at an angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis passing trough fixed end, then the elongation of the spring will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The particle is moving in a horizontal circle, so it is accelerated towards the centre with magnitude& $\dfrac{v2}{r}$.~The horizontal force on the particle is due to the spring and is given by~$kx$,~where $x$~is the elongation and $k$ is the spring constant.

$kx = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} = m{ω}^{2}r = m{ω}^{2} \left({l}_{0} +x\right)$

$⇒ \left(k - m{ω}^{2}\right)x = m{ω}^{2}{l}_{0}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{m{ω}^{2}{l}_{0}}{k - m{ω}^{2}}$

$

questions.q: A particle is moving with uniform speed along the circumference of a circle of radius $R$ under the action of a central fictitious force $F$ which is inversely proportional to $R^{3}$. Its time period of revolution will be given by :
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A coin is placed on a disc. The coefficient of friction between the coin and the disc is $\mu$. If the distance of the coin from the center of the disc is $r$, the maximum angular velocity which can be given to the disc, so that the coin does not slip away, is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Normal force acting on the coin is, $N = mg$.

Required friction force to provide centripetal force for the coin is, $f = m{ω}^{2}r$ and maximum value of static friction force available is, $f = \muN = \mumg$.

For limiting condition, we can write

$⇒ \mumg = mr{ω}^{2}$

$⇒ \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mug}{r}}$

questions.q: A mass of $10$ kg is suspended by a rope of length $4m$, from the ceiling. A force $F$ is applied horizontally at the mid-point of the rope such that the top half of the rope makes an angle of $45 °$ with the vertical. Then $F$ equals: (Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ and the rope to be massless)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the tension in the string is& $T$.

Applying the condition of equilibrium in the vertical~direction,

$Tcos \left(45 °\right) = 100$

$⇒ $\dfrac{T}{2} =$100$~ ~$. . . \left(1\right)$

In the horizontal~direction,

$Tsin \left(45 °\right) = F$

$⇒ \dfrac{T}{2} =F$

Put~the value of~$T$~from~equation~\left(1\right)$,

$⇒ F = 100N$

So, the horizontal force applied on the rope will be~$100N$.

$

questions.q: A car of $800 \mathrm{~kg}$ is taking turn on a banked road of radius $300 \mathrm{~m}$ and angle of banking $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$. If coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely:  \left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \sqrt{3}=1.73\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=800 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{r}=300 \mathrm{~m} \\ & \theta=30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \\ & \mu_{\mathrm{s}}=0.2 \\ & \mathrm{~V}_{\max }=\sqrt{\operatorname{Rg}\left[\frac{\tan \theta+\mu}{1-\mu \tan \theta}\right]} \\ & =\sqrt{300 \times \mathrm{g} \times\left[\frac{\tan 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}+0.2}{1-0.2 \times \tan 30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}}\right]} \\ & =\sqrt{300 \times 10 \times\left[\frac{0.57+0.2}{1-0.2 \times 0.57}\right]} \\ & \mathrm{V}_{\max }=51.4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two identical blocks $A$ and $B$ each of mass $m$ resting on the smooth horizontal floor are connected by a light spring of natural length $L$ and spring constant $K$. A third block $C$ of mass $m$ moving with a speed $v$ along the line joining $A$ and $B$ collides with $A$.The maximum compression in the spring is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$C$ comes to rest

${V}_{cm}$ of $A \text{ and } B = \dfrac{v}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}$ is ${v}_{ret}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2}$

$x = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu \times v^{2}}{k}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2k}} \times v$.

questions.q:
A hanging mass $M$ is connected to a four times bigger mass by using a string pulley arrangement, as shown in the figure. The bigger mass is placed on a horizontal ice-slab and being pulled by $2Mg$ force. In this situation, tension in the string is $\dfrac{x}{5}Mg$ for $x =_____. Neglect mass of the string and friction of the block (bigger mass) with ice slab.
(Given $g = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equation for& $4M: 2Mg - T = 4Ma . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation for~$M: T - Mg = Ma . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding both equation we get,

$Mg = 5Ma ⇒ a = \dfrac{g}{5}$

Now, tension~$T = Mg + Ma = \dfrac{6Mg}{5}$

Therefore,~$x = 6$

questions.q: Three blocks $M_1, M_2, M_3$ having masses $4 \mathrm{~kg}, 6 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ respectively are hanging from a smooth pully using rope 1,2 and 3 as shown in figure. The tension in the rope $1, T_1$ when they are moving upward with acceleration of $2 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ is _____\mathrm{N}\left(\right.$ if $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 ).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
FBD of $M_1$ :
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1-200=(4+6+10) \times 2 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{T}_1=240 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two blocks ($m = 0 . 5kg$ and $M = 4 . 5kg$) are arranged on a horizontal frictionless table as shown in the figure. The coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is $\dfrac{3}{7} .$ Then the maximum horizontal force that can be applied on the larger block so that the blocks move together is $N .$ (Round off to the Nearest Integer) [Take $g$~as $9 . 8ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A curved in a level road has a radius $75m$. The maximum speed of a car turning this curved road can be $30ms^{- 1}$ without skidding. If radius of curved road is changed to $48m$ and the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road remains same, then maximum allowed speed would be _____~ $ms^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum speed is given as& $v = \sqrt{\mugr}$, where,~$\mu$~is coefficient of friction and~$r$~is radius of curved road.

$⇒ \dfrac{v1}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{r1}{r2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{30}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{75}{48}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{16}} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = 24ms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
In a spring gun having spring constant $100Nm^{- 1}$ a small ball $B$ of mass $100g$ is put in its barrel (as shown in figure) by compressing the spring through $0 . 05m$. There should be a box placed at a distance $d$ on the ground so that the ball falls in it. If the ball leaves the gun horizontally at a height of $2m$ above the ground. The value of $d$ is $m$.
\left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{2}kx^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
$Kx^{2} = mv^{2}$
$v = x\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} = 0 . 05\sqrt{\dfrac{100}{0 . 1}} = 0 . 05 \times 10\sqrt{10}$
$v = 0 . 5\sqrt{10}$
From $h = \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$
$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 2}{10}} = \dfrac{2}{10}$
$∴ d = vt = 0 . 5\sqrt{10} \times \dfrac{2}{10} = 1m$
